After watching The Ghosts in Our Machine, a documentary about animals and their role in today's society as food, fur, etc., I found myself in the New York area and decided to visit the Farm Sanctuary mentioned many times in the film. I thought some of you who have seen this movie, or know anything about this sanctuary might be interested to hear my experience, so here it is!

This sanctuary, for those of you not familiar, rescues animals from both the meat and dairy industry. Their goal is to not only rescue these animals but to use their stories to inform the public on the cruel experiences that we unknowingly condone every day by eating animals, wearing fur, things like that. They have visiting hours each weekend in the spring, and I think they have expanded visiting hours in the summer. My friends and I decided to take a guided tour around the farm, where we got to meet and interact with different animals. The tour starts with a short video about their organization and what exactly they are saving their animals from. They briefly summarize the cruelties these animals face in slaughterhouses and factory farms. They also have life-size examples of the cages these animals live in, which I found particularly interesting. After the video, we were led to the different locations around the property that house these rescued animals. It was wonderful to see all the different creatures with tons of free space and loving care. We also got to pet some of the animals - the pigs and cows - and were able to feed some of the chickens and hens. Our tour guide was very good about sharing information as we went along, and I actually learned some new things about the industry I didn't know before. Everyone working there was very friendly and they all seemed really invested and educated on each animal's needs.

At the end of the tour, we went back to the visiting center where we had initially started out, and they had a cute gift shop where we each got some things. The sanctuary had a lot of different vegan cookbooks, as well as other literature about living a plant-based lifestyle. They also had a nice brochure on vegan restaurants in the area which was super helpful.

Overall it was a lovely visit, and I am so glad I had the opportunity to go there. The land was beautiful, and seeing so many happy animals was really a treat. I would highly recommend that if you ever find yourself in the Upstate New York area, to pay them a visit. Also their website is super informative so I'll link it here if you wanna check it out.
